title: The Milky Way and our sun
subject: Earth & space

OpenStax Astronomy 2e, 25.1 The Architecture of the Galaxy
OpenStax Astronomy 2e, 25.3 The Mass of the Galaxy
OpenStax Astronomy 2e, 24.6 Evidence for Black Holes
OpenStax Astronomy 2e, 1.6 A Tour of the Universe

steps.title: Bulge
steps.instruction: Trace the bright bulge in the middle.

note.text: The Milky Way is our galaxy: hundreds of billions of stars, plus gas and dust. Stars crowd together in its central bulge.

steps.title: Spiral arms
steps.instruction: Trace the two big spiral arms.

note.text: Seen from above, the disk has spiral arms where gas and dust collect and new stars form.

steps.title: Black hole
steps.instruction: Dab a dot for the black hole at the center.

note.text: At the very center is a black hole with about 4 million times the mass of the sun.
note.remember: A giant black hole sits at the center.

steps.title: The sun
steps.instruction: Dab a dot for the sun.

note.text: Our sun sits about 26,000 light-years from the center, in a small arm between two big ones.

steps.title: The sun's orbit
steps.instruction: Trace the sun's path around the center, with its arrow.

note.text: The sun, carrying the whole solar system with it, orbits the center once every 225 million years.

steps.title: Gravity
steps.instruction: Draw the arrow from the sun toward the center.

note.text: Gravity from all the mass inside the sun's orbit pulls it toward the center, bending its path into an orbit.

steps.title: Edge-on
steps.instruction: Trace the galaxy as it looks from the side.

note.text: From the side, the disk is very thin, like a CD: about 2,000 light-years thick.

steps.title: Bulge from the side
steps.instruction: Trace the bulge bulging out of the disk.

note.text: The bulge is thicker than the disk around it.

steps.title: Width
steps.instruction: Draw the line across the whole disk.

note.text: The disk is about 100,000 light-years across. Light would take 100,000 years to cross it.

steps.title: Gravity's role
steps.question: What keeps the sun and other stars orbiting the center instead of flying off into space?

options.text: Gravity from the galaxy's mass, pulling toward the center
options.feedback: Yes. The same force that holds planets around the sun holds stars in orbit around the galaxy's center.
The arms don't push stars. Gravity pulling toward the center keeps them in orbit.
Stars do move. The sun orbits the center every 225 million years.
The black hole is only a small part of the mass. Gravity from all the mass inside the orbit holds stars in.

steps.title: Scale
steps.question: How is the Milky Way like the solar system?

options.text: In both, gravity pulls objects toward the center and keeps them in orbit
options.feedback: Right. Planets orbit the sun and stars orbit the galaxy's center, both held by gravity.
The galaxy is unimaginably bigger: hundreds of billions of stars, each maybe with planets.
The solar system has one star; the galaxy has hundreds of billions.

options.text: Both have a black hole at the center
options.feedback: The solar system has the sun at its center. Gravity is what they share.
